items.title: 特朗普據報將赴機場迎接習近平，待遇比肩教宗和赫魯曉夫
items.description: 美國總統親赴機場迎接外國元首極為罕見。若不計教宗訪美的特例，這將是超過 60 年來美國總統首次以這種方式迎接他國元首。
items.content:
特朗普據報機場親迎習近平：禮遇比肩教宗與赫魯曉夫，中美外交禮賓慣例解讀
路透社、彭博社等多家通訊社報導，一名美國高級官員週五（9月18日）向記者透露，美國總統特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）計劃下週親赴華盛頓郊外的安德魯斯聯合基地（Joint Base Andrews），迎接前來進行國事訪問的中國國家主席習近平。
國事訪問的禮賓程序高度程式化，但程式之中仍留有彈性空間，足以傳遞微妙的政治信號。東道國接機官員的級別，歷來是觀察雙邊關係溫度最直接的風向標。
美國總統親赴機場迎接外國元首極為罕見。若不計教宗訪美的特例，這將是超過 60 年來美國總統首次以這種方式迎接他國元首。
這一決定發生在中美關係仍處於貿易摩擦和科技競爭陰影之下的時刻，其象徵意義因此格外受到關注。以下從歷史先例、中美互動禮賓變化，以及習近平近年出訪所獲接待規格三個層面，梳理這次安排背後的外交邏輯。
美國總統機場迎賓：歷史上有多罕見
美國總統親赴機場迎接來訪元首，並非從未發生，但案例集中在特定年代。
肯尼迪總統圖書館的資料顯示，1960年代，時任總統肯尼迪（John F. Kennedy）曾多次親自到安德魯斯空軍基地迎接來訪的外國元首，迎接對象包括加納總統恩克魯瑪（Kwame Nkrumah）、突尼斯總統布爾吉巴（Habib Bourguiba）、秘魯總統普拉多（Manuel Prado）、厄瓜多爾總統阿羅塞梅納（Carlos Julio Arosemena）、幾內亞總統塞古·杜爾（Ahmed Sékou Touré）、以及印度總理尼赫魯（Jawaharlal Nehru）等。
但與現在不同的是，肯尼迪執政初期，與其說去接機，其實是因為把歡迎儀式直接放在機場舉行。
在肯尼迪執政後期，頻繁穿越華盛頓迎到機場迎接，時常造成交通擁堵，所以他就改革了這個禮賓儀式，正式確定白宮南草坪為外賓抵達的正式歡迎舞台。此後，外賓飛抵安德魯斯空軍基地之後，由禮賓司長接機並乘直升飛機直抵白宮，再由總統在南草坪舉行歡迎儀式。這成為了美國的外交慣例。
因此，更有可比性的是1959年，時任總統艾森豪威爾（Dwight D. Eisenhower）親自到安德魯斯空軍基地，在舷梯下迎接蘇聯最高領導人赫魯曉夫（Nikita Khrushchev）。而且這在當時也被事先公開和廣泛報道，被視為冷戰下微妙且罕見的禮遇。
不過近年來，在禮賓安排上，羅馬天主教教宗是例外：1987年，里根（Ronald Reagan）在邁阿密機場迎接教宗若望保祿二世（Pope John Paul II）；1999 年，克林頓（Bill Clinton）在機場迎接再次迎接教宗若望保祿二世（Pope John Paul II）；2008年，小布什（George W. Bush）夫婦在安德魯斯空軍基地迎接教宗本篤十六世（Pope Benedict XVI）；2015年，奧巴馬（Barack Obama）夫婦在安德魯斯聯合基地迎接教宗方濟各（Pope Francis）。
過去11年間，再無教宗訪美。
與中方接待特朗普的規格相比
白宮傳出的消息若果屬實，則美方此次安排，規格已超過中方今年5月接待特朗普時的水平。當時特朗普抵達北京，到機場迎接的是國家副主席、前中共中央政治局常委韓正。
特朗普第一任期訪華時，接機人是時任中共中央政治局委員、國務委員楊潔篪。楊潔篪當時在中國外事領域擁有實際決策權，屬於「黨和國家領導人」序列，規格已屬較高。
美國總統在中方接待序列中，歷來享有比一般外國首腦更高的禮遇。多數外國元首訪華時，接機官員通常為部長級，例如德國總理默茨（Friedrich Merz）、英國首相斯塔默（Keir Starmer）訪華時，分別由外交部副部長和財政部長接機。
值得一提的是，根據白宮向記者們透露的行程顯示，習近平的夫人彭麗媛將陪同他一起訪問美國，也算是釋放友善信號，因為在5月份特朗普訪華時，夫人梅拉尼婭·特朗普（Melania Trump）並未隨行。
中國如何接待外國領導人
俄羅斯總統普京（Vladimir Putin）訪華時，享有與美國總統類似級別的接待。今年5月，由中共中央政治局委員、外交部長王毅接機；2025年8月赴天津出席上海合作組織峰會時，則由政治局委員、中共天津市委書記陳敏爾接機。
朝鮮最高領導人金正恩訪華時，曾由中共中央政治局常委王滬寧親自迎接，七常委之一出面接機極為罕見。但這一待遇延續的是中朝之間源自冷戰年代的同盟式「兄弟情誼」，並不屬於中國對外接待的常規序列。
在常規外交框架之外，歷史上有兩次美國總統訪華所獲接待規格超過了普京和金正恩。1972年尼克松（Richard Nixon）「破冰之旅」訪華，當時中美尚未建交，國務院總理周恩來親赴機場迎接，規格之高至今未被超越。
另一次是2009年奧巴馬首次訪華，接機的是時任國家副主席習近平。彼時習近平身兼中共中央政治局常委與國家副主席，且已被公認為接班人，這一安排被普遍視為超規格禮遇。
到了奧巴馬第二任期，美國推出「亞洲再平衡」戰略，中美關係出現波折，接機人選隨即降為外交部長王毅。接機人選的升降，由此成為觀察中美關係走向的晴雨表之一。
習近平經歷過的領導人接機
近年來，習近平出訪時獲外國領導人親自接機，已不算罕見事件。
最近一次是今年6月8日訪問朝鮮時，金正恩親自到機場迎接。這延續了中國領導人訪朝的傳統：此前胡錦濤、江澤民出訪朝鮮，乃至更早年代周恩來以總理身份訪朝時，均由朝鮮最高領導人親自到機場迎接。
其他國家由元首親赴機場迎接習近平的情況也時有發生，但通常需滿足兩個條件：一是與中國關係密切，二是國家體量較小。2024年習近平訪問塞爾維亞時，總統武契奇（Aleksandar Vučić）到停機坪迎接；同年訪問匈牙利時，總理歐爾班（Viktor Orbán）到機場迎接；2025年訪問柬埔寨時，國王西哈莫尼（Norodom Sihamoni）在機場迎接。
更早的一個特殊案例發生在2014年7月。習近平在赴巴西出席金磚國家領導人峰會途中，在希臘羅德島作技術經停。技術經停通常只涉及加油和短暫休整，並不安排正式外交活動。然而希臘時任總統帕普利亞斯（Karolos Papoulias）與總理薩馬拉斯（Antonis Samaras）專程從雅典飛赴羅德島，在機場迎接習近平並舉行會談。兩國最高領導人跨城出迎一次過境停留，極為罕見。
這次超規格接待，背景是希臘當時仍深陷歐債危機，經濟和就業形勢嚴峻，又受到國際紓困計劃的嚴厲財政約束，急需外來投資和基礎設施項目支撐復甦。習近平此行距他提出「一帶一路」倡議僅約十個月。此次會晤後，中希兩國經貿合作明顯提速：兩年後的2016年，中遠海運取得比雷埃夫斯港運營商的控股權，並持續加大對該港口的開發投入。
國際通訊社透露的習近平訪美行程一覽
9月23日（週三）
習近平及夫人彭麗媛抵達安德魯斯聯合基地。
特朗普親赴機場迎接，雙方在該軍事基地舉行抵達歡迎儀式，這在安德魯斯聯合基地同樣極為少見。
9月24日（週四）：會談與國宴
特朗普將在白宮迎接習近平與彭麗媛。
雙方隨後移步玫瑰園，進行儀仗檢閱，再展開雙邊會談。
梅拉尼婭·特朗普與彭麗媛將出席在華盛頓地區舉行的另一場活動，白宮尚未公布具體細節。
晚間，特朗普夫婦將在白宮東廳為習近平與彭麗媛舉辦國宴。特朗普與習近平將在晚宴開始時分別致辭，出席嘉賓包括科技與金融界高管。
9月25日（週五）：茶敘、參觀與離境
特朗普夫婦將在白宮為習近平與彭麗媛舉辦茶敘。
雙方隨後前往華盛頓國家檔案館，參觀美國建國文獻。
習近平與彭麗媛啟程返回安德魯斯聯合基地，隨後離境。

items.title: 香港首任特首董建華葬禮：規格比照霍英東 石泰峰致悼詞
items.description: 香港回歸後首任行政長官董建華周日（9月20日）在香港舉行公祭及出殯儀式。中國國家主席習近平和多名中共政治局常委以不同形式致哀，但並未親自出席。作為首位離世的香港特首，董建華獲得的國家級治喪安排不僅是對其個人政治生涯的評價，也為未來香港前特首的身後禮遇樹立先例。
items.content:
香港首任特首董建華葬禮：規格比照霍英東 石泰峰致悼詞
香港特別行政區首任行政長官董建華的公祭及出殯儀式，周日（9月20日）在香港舉行。中國國家主席習近平及多名中共政治局常委並未親自出席，但以致送花圈、發表唁電等不同形式表達哀悼。中共中央政治局委員、全國政協常務副主席石泰峰奉命出任治喪委員會主任，代表中央赴港主持喪禮。
董建華於9月8日因病逝世，享年89歲。作為香港回歸後首位離世的行政長官，他的身後安排具有指標意義：這不僅是北京對其個人政治生涯的蓋棺論定，也將成為未來歷任香港特首身後禮遇的參照範本。
治喪委員會由石泰峰牽頭，副主任委員包括全國政協副主席梁振英、全國政協副主席兼秘書長王東峰，中央港澳工作領導小組副組長、國務院港澳事務辦公室主任夏寶龍，以及現任香港行政長官李家超。
儀式由梁振英主持，僅限受邀人士出席，靈柩覆蓋中華人民共和國國旗，靈堂懸掛「沉痛悼念董建華先生」橫幅。石泰峰在悼詞中稱董建華為「『一國兩制』的傑出貢獻者」「著名的愛國人士」「傑出的社會活動家」及「中國共產黨的親密朋友」。
儘管沒有任何中共中央政治局常委親臨現場，但從主持治喪的官員級別和悼詞措辭，都使其禮遇與二十年前另一場被稱為「國葬」的告別儀式，即已故全國政協副主席霍英東的葬禮規格相仿。
為何派石泰峰？
董建華的葬禮規格並非無先例可循，因為他離世前最高級別是全國政協副主席，即中國的「副國級」，因此可參照香港另外兩位已故全國政協副主席霍英東、安子介的先例，即由全國政協第一副主席（通常也稱「常務副主席」）來主導和致辭。
石泰峰在中央的政治份量，早前已受到外界關注。
BBC中文網此前報道，他於2025年4月由中央統戰部部長轉任中央組織部部長，同時繼續兼任全國政協常務副主席及政協黨組副書記。
這一安排頗不尋常：政協副主席一職通常由統戰部部長兼任，而石泰峰轉崗關鍵的中組部長後，後仍保留此職。
這意味著，目前石泰峰同時掌握多重要職：中央組織部部長，負責考核和提拔中共高級幹部，是全黨最核心的人事權力機構；全國政協常務副主席兼黨組副書記，主導政協日常運作；以及全國政協黨建工作領導小組組長，掌管政協系統的黨建與幹部管理。
對比霍英東葬禮
香港主權移交以來，僅有少數香港領袖人物身後獲得中央最高規格禮遇，2000年逝世的安子介與2006年逝世的霍英東均屬此列。若論規格與政治象徵意義，外界普遍將董建華此次葬禮，與2006年霍英東逝世後的治喪安排相提並論。
霍英東生前是全國政協副主席，其葬禮雖未被官方明言規格，但因出席人員級別之高，在香港商界人士中極為罕見，社會普遍視之為「國葬」。
當年代表中央赴港主持治喪委員會的是時任全國政協副主席王忠禹，中共中央最高領導層集體致送花圈，包括胡錦濤、江澤民、吳邦國、溫家寶、賈慶林，各中央機構亦分別敬獻花圈。
霍英東靈柩同樣覆蓋國旗，扶靈名單多達十人，包括董建華本人、許仕仁、鄭萬通、李兆基、何鴻燊、朱經武、曾憲梓、陳佐洱、朱維群及高祀仁。
兩場葬禮均出現國旗覆棺、由全國政協系統主導治喪工作的共同安排。
但二十年過去，北京對董建華的定位已不止於愛國商人或全國政協領導人，而多了「香港回歸後首任行政長官」這一歷史角色。目前董建華喪禮的扶靈名單尚未公布，從現場照片看，也未見到中共中央總書記或其他政治局常委以個人名義署名的花圈。
各方對董建華評價
多名受邀出席喪禮的人士，向本地媒體回顧了對董建華的印象。行政會議召集人葉劉淑儀表示：「好難過，董先生是個偉大領袖，我們也很懷念他，他為香港做了很多事，他離任後仍創辦中美交流基金會及相關智庫，繼續出謀獻策。每當香港遇著危難時，他都發聲，愛國愛港，是我們的典範。」
全國政協常委邱達昌則說：「有國旗蓋過他（靈柩），石泰峰先生也很詳細地講述董先生對整個國家、香港的貢獻，是『一國兩制』的第一個支持者，發揮得很好。不論是『八萬五』、中醫港、科技城，都是當時時間的問題，其實長遠對香港也是絕對正確，我覺得董先生絕對是一個好人。」
9月9日，中共中央港澳工作辦公室、國務院港澳事務辦公室發表對董建華的官方悼詞，其歷史定位相當明確：「『一國兩制』的傑出貢獻者、著名的愛國人士、傑出的社會活動家以及中國共產黨的親密朋友」。悼詞高度肯定董建華對香港主權移交後政治秩序的奠基貢獻，稱其「一生愛國至誠、愛港至深、胸懷大局、立場堅定，為香港順利回歸與平穩過渡和『一國兩制』成功實踐作出重大的歷史性貢獻」，並提及他在任內的口頭禪：「香港好，國家好；國家好，香港更好」。
現任特首李家超此前已透過新華社發表聲明「沉痛哀悼」，稱「董建華先生一生以『報效國家，服務香港』為己任，我對董建華先生的辭世深感哀痛，他畢生為香港所作的巨大貢獻將永存我們心中。我謹代表香港特區，向他的家人致以深切慰問。」特區政府亦轉發歷任特首的悼念聲明。
董建華的繼任者曾蔭權說：「回歸後跟隨董先生工作，我親身體會到他忘我的工作精神，終年無休，即使在周末亦心繫公務、夙夜匪懈。」
梁振英則表示：「董先生宅心仁厚，以理服人，為我輩典範。請董先生安息。」
林鄭月娥的聲明說：「對我這位浙江舟山同鄉的後輩，董先生是位十分慈祥的長者，在他家中閒話家常是多麼令人懷念啊！向董建華先生致以最崇高的敬意，最深切的悼念！」
英國駐香港總領事館也發表聲明，對董建華逝世表示「誠摯哀悼」，並提到「董先生與英國淵源深厚，曾負笈利物浦大學修讀海事工程，並畢生支持利物浦足球會」「董先生於香港歷史關鍵時期投身公共服務，其貢獻將為後世銘記」。董建華逝世後，多家政府網站及本地媒體主頁一度轉為黑白色，以示哀悼。
生平：從航運世家到特區首任特首
董建華原本並非職業政治家。他1937年生於上海，1940年代隨家人移居香港，其父董浩雲創辦的東方海外航運集團，曾是全球最大的華資航運企業之一。畢業於英國利物浦大學工程系後，董建華先赴美國工作，其後返港接手家族生意，並在1980年代全球航運業低潮期間帶領企業渡過財務危機，因此在香港商界建立聲譽。
上世紀90年代，中英就香港前途問題展開最後階段談判，北京開始物色香港回歸後特區首任領導人。具有商界背景、立場親北京且熟悉國際事務的董建華逐漸進入中央視野。1996年，他在推選委員會選舉中勝出，成為香港特別行政區首任行政長官，並於1997年7月1日香港主權移交當天正式就職。
董建華八年任期恰逢香港面對一連串重大挑戰：亞洲金融風暴、樓市長期下跌，以及2003年的SARS疫情。
與此同時，作為「一國兩制」實施後的首位行政長官，他也需要在中央政府與香港社會之間尋找平衡。
支持者認為，他在回歸後的關鍵時期承擔了歷史責任，為特區制度運作奠定基礎。
批評者則指出，他未能有效回應社會對民主發展的訴求，其推動《基本法》23條立法更引發回歸後首次大規模民眾抗議。

items.title: 聯合國專家：有理由相信美國在伊朗襲擊行動中犯下戰爭罪
items.description: 美國並未承認曾發動今年2月造成重大傷亡的襲擊，目標包括米納卜（Minab）一所小學及拉梅爾德（Lamerd）一個體育綜合設施。
items.content:
聯合國專家：有理由相信美國在伊朗襲擊行動中犯下戰爭罪
  - Author, 大衛·格里頓（David Gritten）
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 3 分鐘
聯合國人權專家表示，有合理理由相信，美國在伊朗發動的兩次襲擊中犯下戰爭罪，事件造成至少177名平民死亡。
由伊朗問題獨立國際事實調查團發布的一份新報告指出，今年2月對米納布（Minab）一所小學及拉梅爾德（Lamerd）一個體育綜合設施發動的導彈襲擊，構成無差別攻擊，並導致平民死亡及民用基礎設施受損。
美國此前否認曾襲擊拉梅爾德，並表示正調查米納布事件的經過。一名美國國務院官員表示，美方不認同報告中的調查結果。
專家還發現，伊朗當局在1月鎮壓大規模反政府示威期間犯下危害人類罪。
他們表示，安全部隊的殺戮行為遍及全部31個省份，其規模「令人震驚且前所未有」。
伊朗方面尚未就有關調查結果作出評論，但該國過去曾否認有關系統性侵犯人權的指控。
事實調查團在周四發表的一份聲明中警告說：「伊朗平民處於兩難境地：一邊是本國政府犯下的嚴重侵犯人權行為和危害人類罪，另一邊是伊朗與美國和以色列之間的致命衝突。」
在提交聯合國人權理事會的最新報告中，事實調查團的三名獨立專家調查了衝突期間兩宗造成最多平民死亡的襲擊事件。
根據當地官員表示，2月28日，美國和以色列對伊朗發動戰爭時，戰斧巡航導彈擊中南部城鎮米納布的沙賈雷赫·塔耶貝赫小學（Shajareh Tayyebeh Primary School），造成至少156人死亡，其中包括120名兒童。
事實調查團專家表示，該小學毗鄰一處同日在襲擊中受波及的伊斯蘭革命衛隊（IRGC）海軍設施，但校舍標識清晰，且沒有資料顯示其被用作軍事用途。
專家表示，根據所蒐集的證據，包括媒體報道指美軍初步調查發現美軍應對事件負責，以及美國是衝突各方中唯一擁有戰斧導彈（Tomahawk）的一方，他們有合理理由相信襲擊該小學的是美國。
專家還認定，該校是「預定打擊目標，所造成的損害並非由偏離目標的襲擊，或對革命衛隊設施攻擊所造成的附帶損害」，並引述生還者稱校舍曾兩度遭到擊中。
美軍至今尚未公布對米納布襲擊事件的調查結果，但美國國防部長皮特·赫格塞斯（Pete Hegseth）曾表示，美軍「絕不會以平民目標為攻擊對象」。
同樣在2月28日，精確打擊導彈（PrSM）在拉梅爾德鎮一個體育綜合設施及住宅區上空散布鎢彈丸雲。根據當地官員表示，事件造成至少21名平民死亡，其中包括7名兒童。
事實調查團專家再次表示，該體育綜合設施標識清晰，且沒有資料顯示其被用作軍事用途。
他們得出結論稱，有合理理由相信這次襲擊是美國實施的，援引的證據包括美國是衝突各方中唯一擁有精確打擊導彈的一方。
美國軍方表示，當天美軍沒有對拉梅爾德實施任何襲擊，並對認定所用武器為精確打擊導彈的報道提出異議。
對於這兩宗事件，事實調查團專家表示，有「合理理由相信，美國犯下發動無差別攻擊的戰爭罪，導致平民傷亡或民用物體受損」。
事實調查團的報告還涵蓋了伊朗當局對2025年12月及2026年1月席捲全國的大規模抗議活動所進行的暴力鎮壓。
專家表示，這次鎮壓較過往的打壓行動出現前所未有的升級，其特徵包括廣泛使用致命武力，導致大規模死亡和受傷，以及大規模拘捕。
他們引述目擊者、醫護人員及死者家屬稱，安全人員部署在屋頂及其他高處位置，向人群發射突擊步槍。
示威者亦因金屬霰彈槍彈丸而頭部、胸部及眼部嚴重受傷，部分人永久失明。
專家表示，隨着鎮壓升級，安全部隊襲擊醫療設施，毆打及拘捕受傷示威者，並拘捕部分醫護人員，令傷者不敢尋求可挽救生命的治療。
他們還發現，抗議期間被拘留的數以萬計的人士遭受酷刑、單獨囚禁，以及被剝奪獲得法律代表的權利。
專家警告稱，政府此後進一步加強對示威者使用死刑，至少29名男子因與騷亂有關的指控而經快速審訊後被處決。
事實調查團的報告指出，由於無法獨立核實鎮壓行動造成的死亡人數，因此未能確認確切數字，但認為有充分理由相信，死亡人數遠高於官方公布的3,000人。伊朗政府稱，其中大部分死者為安全部隊成員或旁觀者。
總部設於美國的人權活動通訊社（Hrana）表示，已確認超過7,000人被殺，幾乎全部為示威者。
事實調查團專家總結指出，伊朗當局在鎮壓期間犯下「多項嚴重侵犯人權行為」，且有關行為構成「危害人類罪中的謀殺、監禁及其他嚴重剝奪人身自由、酷刑，以及其他不人道行為，而這些行為均是針對平民人口的大規模及有系統攻擊的一部分」。
伊朗當局指控美國和以色列煽動騷亂，並將死亡事件歸咎於其所稱的「恐怖分子」和「暴徒」。

items.title: 「運動員無法伸直雙腿睡覺」：日本亞運為何爆發住宿爭議？
items.description: 亞運選手將入住木製貨櫃屋或一艘意大利郵輪。韓國代表團批評，貨櫃屋宿舍水管漏水，且床舖太小，運動員甚至無法伸直雙腿睡覺。
items.content:
「運動員無法伸直雙腿睡覺」：日本亞運為何爆發住宿爭議？
  - Author, 郭悠（Koh Ewe）
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 2 分鐘
日本亞洲運動會將於週六（9月19日）開幕，住宿問題成為外界激烈批評的焦點。
其中，為數千名運動員而設的木製貨櫃屋，賽前被指漏水和床舖太小。
「身高超過兩米（6呎7吋）的運動員，甚至無法在床上把腿伸直，這實在不合理。」韓國籃球協會副會長鄭載龍（音譯Jung Jae-yong）說。
他向法新社形容，這些住宿設施是「歷來最差的」。
本屆賽事於名古屋市及愛知縣舉行，超過1.7萬名運動員及官員出席，比原先預計的人數多了2000人，過去數週以來外界都擔心床位不足。
漏水的貨櫃屋
木製貨櫃屋將容納約2000人，並設計為日後可重複用作災害疏散設施，但一直飽受批評。
韓國籃球隊一名成員上傳影片，顯示房間內有水管漏水及地面積水，並附上文字：「請幫幫我。」
上週名古屋遭遇破紀錄降雨並引發大範圍水災後，入住貨櫃屋的運動員亦曾短暫疏散。一些比賽場館亦傳出漏水情況。
籃球官員鄭載龍向法新社表示，其他參賽國家代表亦有相同住宿方面的憂慮。
印度當局甚至搭建了這些貨櫃屋的複製版本，讓本國運動員預先適應相關住宿環境。
亞運住宿事務負責人松雄裕太（Yuta Matsuo）向路透社表示，主辦方「充分了解各代表團提出的不滿及憂慮」，強調正「採取具體措施改善運動員的住宿環境」。
有別於奧運會通常設有專屬選手村，亞運的主辦單位選擇以臨時住宿設施安置參賽者。
除貨櫃屋外，另有4000至5000名參賽者將入住一艘意大利郵輪。該郵輪已於週二停靠名古屋，其餘與會人士則將入住酒店。
大會最初預計，將有1.5萬名運動員及官員參加本屆亞運會。但亞洲奧林匹克理事會於8月中旬表示，在新增結合足球與桌球元素的桌式足球（teqball）及板式網球（padel）項目後，參與人數將接近1.7萬人。
亞運組委會主席兼愛知縣知事大村秀章（Hideaki Omura）此前表示，當局原本只為1.5萬人編列預算，對於新增運動員「既沒有足夠人力，也沒有足夠預算作出必要安排」。
他說：「根本沒有地方讓他們住宿。如果他們仍希望前來，就必須自行安排。」
不過，上月主辦方與亞洲奧林匹克理事會表示，所有於7月截止日期前完成報名的「超過1.7萬名」運動員及官員，均已獲提供「符合亞運標準的住宿安排」。
聲明表示：「所有最後準備工作均按計劃進行，且進展順利。本屆亞運會有望成為數十年來最精彩的一屆。」
菲律賓奧林匹克委員會主席托倫蒂諾（Abraham Tolentino）向法新社表示，雖然所有菲律賓運動員都已獲安排床位，但部分官員及教練則入住「不同的酒店和Airbnb」。
本屆亞洲運動會將於週六（9月19日）正式揭幕，並於10月4日閉幕。目前，籃球及足球賽事已經展開。
我們使用了人工智慧協助翻譯這篇文章，它的原文是英文。在發佈之前，BBC記者檢查了翻譯的內容。

items.title: 澳洲收緊移民政策：管制留學生、背包客，打擊「簽證跳轉」
items.description: 澳洲政府希望在2028年前，將海外淨移民人數降至22.5萬人。
items.content:
澳洲收緊移民政策：管制留學生、背包客，打擊「簽證跳轉」
  - Author, 拉娜·林（Lana Lam）
  - Reporting from, 悉尼（Sydney）
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 3 分鐘
澳洲政府宣布收緊移民政策，重點管制國際學生和背包客，並打擊所謂的「簽證跳轉者」（visa hoppers）。
外國學生今後將不得攜帶家屬赴澳，而希望延長居留的人士則必須選擇攻讀更高層級的學位資格。「打工度假簽證」（working holiday visa；工作假期簽證）也將引入抽籤制度。
澳洲內政部長伯克（Tony Burke）在週四（9月17日）發表題為「管理移民計劃的工作：誰到來、誰留下、誰離開」的演講，公布一系列改革措施。
他表示，雖然移民是澳洲的一項「優勢」，但仍需要維持「高度管控」。澳洲政府希望在2028年前，將海外淨移民人數降至22.5萬人。
打擊「簽證跳轉」
談及國際學生及畢業生簽證時，伯克表示：「我們將不再讓學生自動擁有攜帶家庭成員來澳的資格。」
他表示，已身在澳洲的外國學生，以及來自太平洋地區和東南亞國家的申請人將獲得豁免。此外，博士生仍可攜帶家屬，因為他們與本科生處於不同的人生階段。
至於學生簽證，他表示政府將打擊「簽證跳轉」（visa hopping）行為，也就是學生完成一項課程後，再申請另一項課程，而後者通常屬於較低等級的資格，有時甚至來自「不那麼正規的教育機構」。
伯克表示，若學生是為了攻讀更高層級資格，仍可獲准繼續留澳。例如完成學士學位後，再攻讀碩士學位。
打工度假簽證須抽籤
打工度假簽證（working holiday visa；工作假期簽證）也將有重大調整。
這類簽證允許18至30歲人士申請，普遍由背包客使用，也是澳洲農業部門的重要勞動力來源，他們可在澳洲工作12個月，並可申請延長至第二及第三年。
目前，簽證持有人必須在第一年於澳洲偏遠地區工作滿三個月，才能取得第二年簽證資格；其後還需再工作六個月，才能取得第三年簽證資格。
根據新措施，符合第二年簽證資格的人士必須參加抽籤，名額上限為4.5萬個，低於去年符合資格的5.7萬人。
第三年簽證的抽籤名額則限制為5,000個，低於去年符合資格的3.1萬人。
由於英澳自由貿易協定，英國打工度假人士不受這些新措施影響。
過去一年增30萬海外移民
澳洲統計局週四公布的最新數據顯示，截至2026年3月止的12個月內，澳洲人口增長1.4%，達到2,790萬人。
有關數字包括出生和死亡人口變化，以及29.21萬人的海外淨移民人數。
隨著生活成本持續上升、住房負擔能力下降，以及公共服務承受更大壓力，澳洲人口規模的討論持續升溫，移民問題仍是重要政治議題。
以反移民立場聞名的右翼民粹政黨「同一國家黨」（One Nation），近月支持度顯著上升。該黨本週稍早公布移民政策，建議在三年內削減75萬個臨時移民簽證。
該黨於今年5月贏得首個聯邦眾議院議席，同時主張將海外淨移民人數上限設為13萬人。伯克批評這一提議，表示有可能「重創澳洲經濟的部分領域」。
今年7月，澳洲政府推出新政策，優先處理在澳洲境內提交的家庭簽證申請，即申請人在遞交申請時已身處澳洲境內，而非在海外提出申請。
已在澳洲境內並申請永久居留簽證的技術移民，也較海外申請人獲得優先處理。
政府同時暫停來自24個國家的打工度假簽證申請，但英國不在此限。
協助新移民在澳洲安頓的國際安置服務機構（Settlement Services International）的維奧萊特・魯梅利奧蒂斯（Violet Roumeliotis）表示，有關移民的辯論愈來愈受到「短期政治考量，而非最有利於國家的事情」所主導。
她說：「針對國際學生家庭簽證所提出的改變，就是一個很好的例子。」
她補充道，這將使澳洲更難與其他國家競爭、吸引「未來的人才」。

items.title: 基民盟已在三场地方选举中失利 默茨宣布无辞职打算
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/基民盟已在三场地方选举中失利-默茨宣布无辞职打算/a-79347413?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 周日（9月20日），德国基民盟在梅克伦堡-前波莫瑞州和城市州柏林举行的地方选举中均遭败绩。根据出口民调，选择党在梅克伦堡-前波莫瑞州地方选举中拔得头筹。左翼党则在柏林大败默茨领导的基民盟。
items.content:
基民盟已在三场地方选举中失利 默茨宣布无辞职打算
2026年9月20日
（德国之声中文网）据出口民调显示，极右翼政党“德国选择党”（AfD）在德国东北部梅克伦堡-前波莫瑞州举行的地方选举中拔得头筹。这一胜利增强了该党在全国范围内的势头。
根据德国公共电视台ARD的出口民调，选择党预计在梅克伦堡-前波莫瑞州获得 37%的选票，领先于获得35.5%选票的中左翼社民党；相比之下，总理默茨所在的保守党基民盟仅获得5.5%的选票，勉强跨过了进入州议会的门槛。
不过，鉴于其他主要政党均排除了与选择党合作的可能性，该极右翼政党不太可能获得执政机会。
如果最终的点票结果与出口民调的预测一致，那将是基民盟自1949年以来在任何州选举中取得的最差成绩。这也是选择党在一个月内第二次在州级选举中获得第一名；尽管该党遭到主流政党的排斥，但在全国民调中却处于领先地位。
在周日举行的另一场选举——首都柏林的选举中，同样根据出口民调，极左翼的左翼党获得了24.5%的选票，成为柏林最强的政治力量。基民盟获得20%的支持，而选择党的实力也有所增强，得票率达到16%。
周日的选举结果未必会给总理默茨带来致命打击，毕竟他上周刚获得了八位保守派州长的支持。
然而，低迷的支持率、不受欢迎的改革措施，加上选择党早些时候在萨克森-安哈尔特州选举中的胜利，使得他的政治前途充满变数。不过默茨周日晚间发表讲话表示，尽管基民盟在梅克伦堡-前波莫瑞州和柏林的州选举中表现不佳，但他仍将继续留任，继续推进他已启动的改革路线。
“我想带领我们的国家向前发展，”默茨在柏林表示，并称德国改革“势在必行”。

items.title: 中美高层纽约会谈 为特朗普习近平峰会铺路
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/中美高层纽约会谈-为特朗普习近平峰会铺路/a-79346677?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 美国财政部长贝森特与中国国务院副总理何立峰20日在纽约举行高层会谈，围绕贸易休战延长、人工智能监管、关键矿产供应及伊朗问题等议题展开磋商，为特朗普与习近平数日后的白宫会晤做准备。分析认为，双方短期内或难取得重大突破，但有望就维持经贸关系稳定、避免紧张局势升级达成有限共识。
items.content:
中美高层纽约会谈 为特朗普习近平峰会铺路
2026年9月20日
（德国之声中文网）据法新社报道，美国财政部长贝森特和中国国务院副总理何立峰周日（9月20日）在摩根大通纽约总部举行会谈，为两国领导人峰会前就贸易、人工智能和关键矿产等问题达成潜在协议奠定基础。
报道称，特朗普的首席贸易官员杰米森·格里尔（Jamieson Greer）也参与这场会谈。预计会议将持续一整天。
此次会谈是计划于周四在白宫举行的世界两大经济体领导人会晤的前奏，届时特朗普总统和中国国家主席习近平将举行会面。
双方将寻求缓解在贸易、技术及其他战略关切领域的紧张局势。这些议题包括可能延长将于11月到期的贸易休战协议，以及制定人工智能发展的“护栏”规则。
贝森特在抵达会谈现场时对记者表示：“我期待今天能进行专注、全面且富有建设性的会谈，为我们领导人的会晤做好准备。”
美国官员还将寻求确保稀土和关键矿产的持续供应，这些物资对美国制造商至关重要。
另一个议题是美国对伊朗施加的经济压力，目前华盛顿与德黑兰之间的冲突已进入第七个月。
中国是伊朗最重要的经济伙伴，购买了伊朗大部分石油产量，也是伊朗重要的外交支持者。
分析人士指出，最可能的结果是华盛顿与北京就一些小步骤达成一致，以表明双方正继续避免在这一对全球经济影响重大的微妙贸易关系中激化紧张局势。
不过分析人士也警告，人们对特朗普与习近平的峰会预期不高。
“短期内我们唯一能期待的就是停火，而且这种停火可能会持续到今年年底。”美国前副国务卿库尔特·坎贝尔表示。
现为华盛顿战略咨询公司亚洲集团首席CEO的坎贝尔补充说：“我认为你会听到总统宣布打算再与习近平会面两次的消息。”
预计特朗普和习近平将于11月在中国深圳举行的亚太经合组织（APEC）论坛上会面。此外，特朗普可能还将邀请习近平参加12月在迈阿密举行的二十国集团（G20）峰会。
贝森特、何立峰和格里尔的此次会晤延续了过去16个月形成的模式，即这三位官员在欧洲和亚洲城市会面，为特朗普和习近平可能达成的协议进行前期筹备。
这些努力包括2025年11月在韩国釜山达成的休战协议。此前，双方关税战不断升级，税率一度飙升至三位数；该休战协议将特朗普对中国商品征收的关税上限设定在约20%。

items.title: 台湾高官罕见赴华 出席APEC会议
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/台湾高官罕见赴华-出席apec会议/a-79345518?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 台湾劳动部长洪申翰周日飞往中国南京，准备出席周一开始的亚太经合组织（APEC）部长级会议。此行颇为罕见，是赖清德政府上台以来的首次部长级访问。亚太经合组织是台湾所属的少数几个国际组织之一。
items.content:
台湾高官罕见赴华 出席APEC会议
2026年9月20日
（德国之声中文网）洪申翰是自赖清德就任台湾总统以来，首位前往中国大陆的台湾高层政府官员。他将出席周一（9月21日）在南京召开的APEC（亚太经济合作组织）人力资源发展部长会议。据中央社报道，这位台湾劳动部长周日下午抵达桃园机场，面对守候的记者，他未受访或发表谈话。
洪申翰曾在9月15日表示，“我们是APEC的正式会员”，称平等参与、对等尊严是一直以来参与APEC最核心的原则，会依照APEC的规定参与、不会自我设限。
台湾劳动部向法新社透露，洪申翰此次行程并无前往中国大陆其他城市的计划。
洪申翰此前曾是民进党立法委员，曾多次就香港、西藏、新疆等人权议题公开表态，批评中国政府侵犯人权。
台湾拥有APEC正式成员资格
中国将台湾视为其领土一部分，并威胁必要时将通过武力“实现统一”。中国将台湾总统赖清德称为 “分裂分子”，近期频繁在台湾周边开展军演。赖清德则表示，只有台湾人民才能决定自己的未来。
APEC由21个成员经济体组成，是台湾拥有正式成员资格的少数几个国际组织之一。
鉴于中国是今年APEC东道主，此前曾有担忧认为台湾可能无法参与这一国际论坛。
不过，此前已有层级较低的台湾官员参加了在中国大陆举行的其他APEC活动，其中包括时任台湾最高经贸谈判代表杨珍妮5月赴苏州出席会议。杨珍妮出席5月22日会议时其桌牌写着“Chinese Taipei”（这也是台湾参加奥运会时使用的名称），与台湾在APEC的会籍名称一致。台湾媒体当时报道强调“未被矮化！”
谁将担任今年台湾的APEC峰会特使？
APEC系列会议将以11月在深圳举行的APEC领导人非正式会议（APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting，通常称为“APEC峰会”）达到高潮。包括中国领导人习近平、美国总统特朗普在内的多国领导人预计都将出席该峰会。
为避免引发政治问题，台湾总统通常不出席领导人峰会，而是派遣前任官员或商界领袖（如芯片巨头台积电创始人张忠谋）代表出席。
台湾尚未宣布谁将作为特使，出席今年11月在深圳的峰会。

items.title: 德国两州地方选举是否成为总理默茨的“生死局”？
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德国两州地方选举是否成为总理默茨的-生死局-？/a-79345122?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 本周日（9月20日），德国梅克伦堡-前波莫瑞州和城市州柏林均举行地方选举。根据选前的民调结果，极右翼和极左翼可能赢得的胜利将带来新的冲击波，并动摇陷入困境的德国总理默茨的政府。
items.content:
德国两州地方选举是否成为总理默茨的“生死局”？
2026年9月20日
（德国之声中文网）两周前，极右翼、亲特朗普且对莫斯科持友好态度的“德国选择党”（AfD）在萨克森-安哈尔特州重创了默茨领导的基民盟，这引发了外界对于基民盟党内对默茨支持动摇的猜测。
默茨的支持率正急剧下滑，他承诺的经济和社会福利改革在推动过程中也步履维艰。
前几日默茨取消了出席联合国大会的行程，以便应对本周日梅克伦堡-前波莫瑞州和柏林的地方选举可能引发的后续冲击。
周日早8点，两个州的各个投票站开始开放，接受选民投票。
“我希望选择党获胜，因为这样他们就必须证明自己：要么能做出一番成绩，要么这将是他们最后一次获得选票。”退休职员彼得·索默（Peter Sommer）在梅克伦堡-前波莫瑞州的一个投票站外告诉法新社记者。
民调显示，选择党将在周日的选举中进一步扩大势力，尽管该党在周日投票的两个州都不太可能触及执政权。9月初在萨克森-安哈尔特州举行的地方选举中，选择党获得约44%的选票，成为该州第一大党，而且仅差几个席位就能获得州议会的绝对多数。
在柏林的一处投票站，43岁的莫里茨·伦布克-奥泽（Moritz Lembke-Oezer）告诉法新社，尽管他担心投票结果可能让选择党受益，但他仍希望基民盟能在这场选举中“受到惩罚”。
“也许到那时默茨就会下台了，”这位土生土长的柏林人说道。他表示计划投票给左翼党，因为该党承诺解决首都严峻的住房危机。
两场投票 不同的挑战
在周日的投票中，基民盟在两个州面临着各不相同的挑战。
在梅克伦堡-前波莫瑞州，默茨所在的基民盟只是个旁观者，真正的角逐是在广受欢迎的州长曼努埃拉·施韦西格（Manuela Schwesig）领导的社民党与选择党之间展开的。
根据德国电视二台的数据，选择党的支持率为36%，紧追社民党的37%；而基民盟支持率仅为6%，处于岌岌可危的边缘——一旦跌破5%的门槛，该党将失去在州议会的席位。
如果基民盟的得票率跌破这一门槛，将是史无前例的惨败，并给默茨带来巨大的压力。
在柏林，执政的基民盟正与左翼党展开一场势均力敌的较量。左翼党承诺采取激进措施解决住房问题，并深受年轻人欢迎。
如果基民盟在此地败北，对默茨而言将是又一次沉重打击——尤其是败给左翼党，因为该党主张遏制企业权力，且立场亲近莫斯科。
默茨于去年5月上任时，曾誓言要重振疲软的经济，重建军事力量以威慑俄罗斯，并减少非正规移民，以此安抚选民的担忧，将他们从选择党手中争取过来。
然而，德国选择党目前在全国民调中领先，而默茨个人的支持率仅徘徊在10%出头。默茨偶尔直率甚至尖刻的言论，也无助于改善这一局面。
支持率跌入谷底
Infratest Dimap研究机构的民调专家罗兰·阿博尔德（Roland Abold）表示，就默茨个人而言，目前的处境相当严峻。
他说：“在9月份的上一轮调查中，仍有13%的人对他的政治表现感到满意。对于一位现任总理来说，这是我们记录到的最低支持率。”
一些评论人士指出，默茨面临的大部分问题都源于外部因素。乌克兰战争和中东冲突导致能源价格飙升，进而加剧了生活成本危机。
与此同时，中国的迅速崛起正将一个德国长期的出口市场转变为激烈的工业竞争对手。

items.title: 墙外文摘：中国国安利用AI细化跨境镇压
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/墙外文摘：中国国安利用ai细化跨境镇压/a-79344971?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 美国人工智能公司Anthropic的调查发现，与中国安全机关相关联的行动者，大量地将Claude用于“维稳”监控与跨国镇压，包括获取境外抗议活动的行动前场地情报。
items.content:
（德国之声中文网）Anthropic 9月10日发布154页的AI滥用报告《侦测与反制AI滥用：2026年9月》，涵盖2025年12月至2026年8月被其阻断的活动。报告说，今年1月至7月，该公司识别并中断了一批有国家关联行为者、国家关联承包商与商业间谍软件供应商利用Claude建立和运行的监控行动，涉及中国、伊朗与西非的行为者。中国一个宗教事务情报搜集单位，过去由多个分析师团队组成，现已缩减为一间办公室，靠AI助手每月产出数千份调查。报告还指出，几乎所有案例中，操作者都是国家关联机构，所针对的正是这些政权历来针对的侨民与异见社群。
另一组编号GTG-14021的账号，被认定与中国某市级公安及国家安全机关相关联，用于“维稳”监控与跨国镇压。报告说，其中一个市级网警单位使用Claude Code与自定义技能运行舆情监控管线、查询政府监控数据库，并生成涉政治敏感事件的日报，其中包括追踪一个知名海外异见账号。
境外活动前的场地情报
Claude曾拒绝生成每周“维稳”报告，但行为者（一名公安侦查员兼警校研究生）重新构造提示后，得到了点名10名普通公民、按“截访”“约谈”“密切监控行动与通讯”等类别列出的处置建议。某地方国安机关则跑了一条日更管线，按政府模板产出“态势感知”简报，并把这套流程写成了一份AI使用手册，其中包含要求Claude扮演“服务于国家安全机关的情报分析员”的提示词。
行为者也曾指示Claude生成针对境外抗议活动的行动前场地情报。其中包括：温哥华一场民主游行的集合点、路线与终点，土耳其的维吾尔文化活动场地，以及奥斯陆自由论坛的放映会。
报告还提到编号GTG-14010的另一起行动，把Claude以外途径抓取来的100多个受监控WhatsApp群组和数十个Telegram频道的聊天内容，通过Claude转为结构化中文数据，根据经济压力、家庭离散与意识形态幻灭来筛选可下手的对象，并特别标出在新疆仍有家人的目标——报告写道，这种筹码只有与中国境内安全部门协同才能动用。
209起酷刑指控，无一人被追责
人权捍卫者网络（CHRD）9月16日发布研究报告《欲盖弥彰：中国政府杜绝酷刑的制度性失败》，分析了2016年至2025年间209名良心犯提出的酷刑及虐待指控，并采访25名人权捍卫者、家属和律师，案例覆盖除澳门以外的全部省区市及香港。
报告发现，警方和监狱管理人员持续普遍使用酷刑，通常为了刑讯逼供。209起指控中约五分之一涉及殴打在押良心犯，有些涉及电击和单独监禁；最常见的形式是剥夺病患者获得适当医疗的权利，占比高达35%，其中至少16人因疾病得不到治疗而死于羁押期间。逾半数指称遭受酷刑者是以"寻衅滋事"罪被监禁的。
报告列举人权律师丁家喜的经历：2019年12月被带走后遭"指定居所监视居住"半年，据其陈述曾连续73天遭审讯、被固定在“老虎凳”上、胸部被束带勒紧以限制呼吸，直到被捕13个月后才获准会见律师。
报告指出，问题不只在酷刑本身，还在于取证与救济之难：讯问场所的录音录像通常完全掌握在有关部门手中。一名受访律师说，自己提出的投诉超过九成没有得到解决，其中95%完全没有任何回应。209起案例中，仅找到法院对丁家喜和黄雪琴两人展开调查的记录，而两案最终均称未发现酷刑证据。该机构表示没有发现任何涉案官员因施加酷刑被刑事起诉或纪律处分，中国政府2025年提交联合国禁止酷刑委员会的报告中也未提供问责数据。

Thousands march in France against ‘licence to kill’ draft law
In July, deputies in the National Assembly approved the bill which says any police official who uses force is assumed to have acted legally
Thousands of people marched in Paris and other French cities on Sunday against a proposed law on the legitimate use of force that critics say would be a “licence to kill” for police and gendarmes.
In July, deputies in the National Assembly approved the bill which says that any police official who uses force is assumed to have acted legally when using their weapon. It now faces a vote in the Senate.
Politicians, rights groups and other activists joined the Paris demonstration, among them Mathilde Panot of the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party.
“The police kill already,” Panot told the crowd, calling for the bill to be voted down in the Senate.

Germany’s Merz vows to press ahead with reforms after historic state election defeat
Exit polls showed Merz’s centre-right Christian Democratic Union coming in with just 5 per cent of the vote in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz suffered a bruising electoral setback in two state elections on Sunday, including a historic defeat for his party, but vowed to press ahead with potentially painful reforms to Europe’s biggest economy.
Exit polls by public broadcaster ARD on Sunday night indicated that Merz’s centre-right Christian Democratic Union, or CDU, came in with just 5 per cent in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania – the lowest result ever since World War II for the party in any state. The anti-migration, Russia-friendly Alternative for Germany (AfD) party made significant gains on Sunday.
Merz acknowledged his party’s result as a “disaster” but struck a defiant note, rejecting any retreat from his government’s reform agenda. He argued that Germany’s economic and political problems made difficult and potentially unpopular reforms more urgent, not less, and pledged to press ahead.
“What needs to be done now requires backbone, steadfastness, and patience,” Merz said in a statement soon after the exit polls were announced on public television. “I will demonstrate these qualities as chairman of the CDU and, above all, as Chancellor of our country.”

UK’s Burnham congratulates Trump and Danish PM on Greenland deal
On Saturday Trump said he had a deal with Denmark to bolster US military presence in Greenland after threatening to take the island by force
Andy Burnham has congratulated Denmark and the United States on a deal to “strengthen security in the Arctic” after the two countries reached an agreement over Greenland.
The Prime Minister and his Danish counterpart Mette Frederiksen “welcomed the US’ commitment to the region” in a call on Sunday morning, Downing Street said.
In a readout, a No 10 spokesperson said: “The two leaders began by discussing their upcoming visits to New York for the UN General Assembly (UNGA). The Prime Minister said he would use the trip to drive forward work on issues that matter to people at home, including reducing the cost of living through greater global stability and delivering security for people through closer international partnerships.”
“Turning to defence and security, the two leaders discussed the forthcoming signing of a new deal to strengthen security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic area between the US, Greenland and Denmark this week,” the spokesperson added.

items.content:
Italy’s Meloni plans to ban burkas, niqabs in schools and cap foreign pupils in classrooms
Those wanting a future in Italy must ‘learn our language’ and ‘respect our rules’, Meloni told the youth wing of her nationalist party
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said on Sunday she will soon introduce a measure to her government that would cap the number of foreign pupils in classrooms and ban the wearing of burkas and niqabs in schools.
Meloni told the youth wing of her nationalist conservative Brothers of Italy party that the measure would also make Italian language lessons compulsory for parents of foreign pupils having “serious difficulties integrating into the school system”.
“For us, anyone who comes to Italy and wants to build their future here must learn our language, understand our culture, and respect our rules,” she said to a standing ovation at the Gioventu Nazionale national festival in Rome. “It is the only serious way to welcome them.”
Meloni specifically referred to a ban on the burka, an all-covering dress worn by some Muslim women, and the niqab, the veil worn by the most conservative Muslim women, in which, at most, only the eyes show. But Meloni did not mention the hijab, the headscarf worn by some Muslim women.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Trade Representative Jamieson Greer held their final preparatory talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York on Sunday to work out deliverables for next week’s summit between Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump in Washington.
The leaders are meeting at JP Morgan’s headquarters in the city to discuss possible economic outcomes for the summit and begin their long-awaited dialogue on artificial intelligence safety and governance.

items.title: German Chancellor Merz calls state election a 'disaster' for his party but vows to stay on
items.description: Exit polls show damaging losses for Merz's centre-right CDU party in the states of Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.
items.content:
German Chancellor Merz calls state election a 'disaster' for his party but vows to stay on
- Published
Embattled German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has vowed to stay on despite exit polls in two local elections suggesting damaging defeats for his centre-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU) party.
In the north-eastern state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, the party was projected to only just scrape into parliament, while the AfD was on track to win the most votes. Merz called the result "a disaster" for his party.
In Berlin, the ruling CDU was also expected to be beaten by Die Linke (The Left).
Merz is under mounting pressure, with poor approval ratings and rumours he could even be replaced mid-term in a so-called chancellor swap.
Votes took place on Sunday, a fortnight after the CDU saw its vote halved as the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) won a major victory in the state of Saxony-Anhalt.
Echoing comments he made after that defeat, Merz told reporters on Sunday that he would forge ahead with his coalition government's plans to push through a package of economic, tax and welfare reforms.
"The reforms have to come," he insisted. "I am taking on this responsibility, because I want to move our country forward".
"I would even go so far as to say that these reforms are the antidote to the authoritarian poison that, with the fascination of authoritarianism, is penetrating ever deeper into our society," Merz added.
As the projected results came up on the screen at the CDU's election night gathering in Berlin, there were no cheers or celebration.
This is a party that knows it's in trouble.
Friedrich Merz is going on the offensive, quickly declaring he is going nowhere.
He has long coveted the top job in German politics and likely won't give it up easily.
Polls for both states closed at 18:00 local time (17:00 BST), with a final result expected in the coming hours.
According to public broadcaster ZDF, the AfD was projected to take 38% of the vote share in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. It was followed in second place by the centre-left SPD, on 36%.
However, the AfD is unlikely to govern in the state as other parties refuse to work with it.
For Berlin, the broadcaster put the CDU on 20% of the vote share when polls closed, behind Die Linke on nearly 26%.
Prior to Sunday's elections, there had been intense speculation in Germany that Merz could be replaced unless his party's political fortunes improved.
Earlier this week, the leaders of eight German states backed Merz, who has only held the post for 16 months.
While his backers have argued that many of the problems the nation faces are inherited, Merz himself is deeply unpopular.
The former corporate lawyer's tack to the right on issues like immigration has failed to erode AfD support while also alienating people further to the left.

items.title: Key takeaways from BBC interview as Earl Spencer defends claims about King
items.description: Earl Spencer speaks to the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg ahead of the publication of his book about his sister Diana, Princess of Wales.
items.content:
Key takeaways from BBC interview as Earl Spencer defends claims about King
- Published
Earl Spencer has told the BBC writing his book about sister Princess Diana, which has made headlines for its criticism of King Charles, was his "duty...as an eyewitness to history".
In an interview with the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg ahead of the memoir's release on Tuesday, Earl Spencer said he wanted "to put things down once and for all that were true".
Among claims made in Swan Song about the King, who was then the Prince of Wales, was that he said "we'll forget her soon enough" during an argument over whether Princes William and Harry should walk in Diana's funeral procession.
In a strongly worded response, Buckingham Palace said the King was "mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgement and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss".
Here are the key moments from Earl Spencer's interview, which include his first account of how he was told about Diana's death and criticism of press coverage of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex.
Earl initially told Diana's crash was 'not too serious'
Earl Spencer was in South Africa when Princess Diana died in a Paris car crash in the early hours of 31 August 1997, along with close friend Dodi Fayed and the driver of the car.
He told the BBC he got a call in the middle of the night from his sister Lady Jane Fellowes, who said Princess Diana had been in a crash but "it's not too serious".
But then he "kept getting more and more distressing calls" from his sister.
"And then my sister Jane said, 'I'm afraid she's died.' It started... as a little prang, and then it became a broken leg, perhaps a head injury, and then death."
Charles had 'giddy tone' after Diana's death
Describing the hours after her death, Earl Spencer said he took a call at his home in Cape Town from Prince Charles, who told him how he broke the news to Princes William and Harry at Balmoral Castle.
"I felt there was a sort of giddy tone," he told the BBC.
"I'd had a lot of calls that day from people who cared, who were stunned... and I just felt there was a lightness in his tone about Diana's death that really jarred with me."
In his book, Earl Spencer compares his tone to like a "lottery winner" and says he suspects the prince's reaction was based on how this event would free him to marry the woman he loved, his future wife Queen Camilla.
When asked by Kuenssberg if he could be sure that is what Prince Charles was thinking, Earl Spencer said: "I cannot be sure, I'm saying that's what I assume from the tone is a possibility."
Comments 'will not be a surprise' to William and Harry
Earl Spencer told the BBC he had been discussing funeral arrangements with a palace official, who said it had been agreed Princes William and Harry should walk behind their mother's coffin. Unhappy, he said he told the official it is not what his sister would have wanted, before the conversation came to an end.
Soon after, the earl says he took a call from Prince Charles, who asked him about his opposition to it.
"I said, 'Well, of course not, sir, she wouldn't want it'. And then he said, 'Well, I walked behind Lord Mountbatten's coffin.' And I said, 'Yes, but you were 30 and he wasn't your mother'."
He then claims Charles went "ballistic... and ranted for a while" about the Spencer's sense of duty not being adequate enough before "he said 'We'll forget her [Diana] soon enough'."
"I really was so stunned and after a stunned silence I said 'I can not believe you just said that' and I hung up on him", the earl told Kuenssberg during his sit down interview at his Althorp estate.
Responding to the Palace's statement pushing back on the story, Earl Spencer said: "I can tell you here and now, those are exactly the words he said.
"I've only ever had two calls on the line with Prince Charles at any stage in my life.
"I was hyper-alert to what he was saying, and those are precisely the words he said. And I promise that to you now. Genuinely, that is what he said.
"I don't hear him saying he didn't say that."
The earl said he told "close friends and family" about the "monstrous" comment.
When asked if people should believe him or the King, he said: "Well, I'm telling the truth... what else would have made me hang up on the King that day?"
On what Princes William and Harry might think of the comments being brought up nearly 30 years later, he added the words "will not be a surprise" to the brothers.
He also said his renowned funeral eulogy, in which he said his sister's qualities would never be "extinguished from our minds", was a "direct rebuttal" of the prince's comments.
'I know lots of things about the King' not in the book
Talking about his motivations for writing the book, Earl Spencer, aged 62, said it was his "duty... as an eyewitness to history" and as someone in the "final season of my life" with his parents dying in their sixties.
"I'm aware of mortality and I wanted to just put things down once and for all that were true," the historian and journalist explained.
"This is not a threat, it's a fact, I know lots of things about the King which I chose not to include in the book because they were not relevant."
When put to him that the statement sounded like a threat when it involved potentially damaging information, he said: "No, not at all a threat, it's just the reality."
Kuenssberg questioned why he included an account of a conversation in which his sister told him Prince Charles was in love with his valet - a claim Earl Spencer said was improbable - and asked if he was motivated in including some of these allegations to create interest to sell the book.
"It's in the context of a conversation where Diana is telling me that her marriage is over," the earl replied.
"It's a brother's tribute, a loving tribute to a sister. And I think she deserves honesty so that's what I've delivered."
Earl Spencer worries about Harry's lack of police protection
When asked about how he thinks Prince Harry has been treated by the Royal Family, Earl Spencer told the BBC he is reluctant to discuss it, but he said he was concerned about his security.
"I would say that I personally worry about the fifth-in-line to the throne who's served in the military not having any police protection," he said.
"As an uncle who's seen his sister die in very, very preventable circumstances, that I would veer towards protection."
It is understood the committee that oversees royal and VIP security, known as Ravec, is to reconsider Prince Harry and Meghan's level of police protection now they and their two children are full-time residents in the UK rather than visitors.
When asked about how the press treated Princess Diana and now Prince Harry and Meghan, he said tabloid articles "could be really really unpleasant".
"It would really be beholden on people to learn from Diana's example. I'm not here to speak for Harry and Meghan, but for anyone who's being destroyed in this way daily, it must be such a cancerous influence in their life," Earl Spencer said.
"[Diana] was really brought low by all that criticism. And yeah I suppose it's a pity when I see echoes of that now."
'I hope William and Harry resolve row'
Earl Spencer said he did not take sides - as he perceives is the "perception in the media" - in the dispute between Princes William and Harry.
"I'm on my deceased sister's sons' side, both of them. And if either of them wanted anything then I'd be equally there for them," he said.
"And I never get involved in one camp or the other, except as a benign figure I hope."
He said there are a "lot of reasons on both sides" why the brothers' relationship had "got to this stage".
"I hope one day it's resolved, but I don't know all – I certainly don't know what's been done in the finer detail and so I would feel intrusive if I got more involved than to say of course a mother would want her two sons to be happy together and love each other," he said.
Diana 'convinced she couldn't trust people' after Bashir interview
Reflecting on the time before Princess Diana's death, Kuenssberg asked if the infamous BBC Panorama interview with journalist Martin Bashir in 1995 might have been linked indirectly to his sister finding herself in Paris in 1997.
Shortly after the interview broadcast, in which Princess Diana admitted having an affair and said Prince Charles's affair with then-Camilla Parker Bowles made her feel worthless, the Queen wrote to Prince Charles and Princess Diana telling them to divorce.
A 2021 inquiry found Bashir acted in a "deceitful" way by mocking up fake bank statements - which falsely suggested individuals were being paid to keep Diana under surveillance - and showing them to Earl Spencer to gain access to the late princess.
Earl Spencer said he did make "a connection" between the crash and the Panorama interview and said they conned both him and Diana.
"People said, 'Oh, she was paranoid'. She wasn't paranoid. She was convinced that she couldn't trust people because the evidence was there. And, you know, I think that left her vulnerable that night."
The BBC and Bashir apologised to King Charles, Earl Spencer and Princes William and Harry after the 2021 report was published.
The BBC's then-director general, Tim Davie, said: "Although the report states that Diana, Princess of Wales, was keen on the idea of an interview with the BBC, it is clear that the process for securing the interview fell far short of what audiences have a right to expect. We are very sorry for this."
Earl supports 'a modern monarchy'
Earl Spencer, the ninth earl of an aristocratic family whose peerage dates back to the 18th Century and retains its vast estate, told the BBC he is "all for a monarchy, but I like a modern monarchy".
Talking about the "jarring" protocol around the monarchy, he said: "You know, you mentioned the statement earlier, 'His Majesty says", I just don't think it's healthy for a human being to be seen in such archaic, servile terms.…

items.title: Watch: Emotional Earl Spencer says he misses sister Diana every day
items.description: "This is my swan song too. I'm not here to bang on about Diana, this is my final word, celebration of her", Earl Spencer told presenter Laura Kuenssberg.
items.content:
Watch: Emotional Earl Spencer says he misses sister Diana every day
Earl Spencer, brother of Diana, Princess of Wales, said he misses his sister every day during an interview with the BBC.
"That's the thing with sibling loss, you never get over it," he told Laura Kuenssberg.
His book, Swan Song: Diana, My Sister, is due to be published on Tuesday and is expected to be highly critical of the Royal Family.
He said one of the reasons the book is called Swan Song is because it is his "sign off" as Diana's brother and "final take on the situation".
"This is my swan song too. I'm not here to bang on about Diana, this is my final word, celebration of her," he added.
The full interview, Princess Diana: My Sister's Story, is available on BBC iPlayer and will be broadcast on BBC One at 18:30 BST on Sunday.

items.title: Largest attack on Moscow sees Ukraine fire hundreds of drones, mayor says
items.description: Moscow's mayor says 450 drones were downed during the overnight barrage, in which two people died.
items.content:
Largest attack on Moscow sees Ukraine fire hundreds of drones, mayor says
- Published
Ukraine has fired its largest drone attack on the Moscow region, the mayor has said, hitting the city's main oil refinery and a residential building.
Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 450 drones heading for the capital had been shot down in what he called "the most massive" attack. The region's governor said at least two people were killed and 20 injured.
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed Kyiv had hit a "key" Russian oil facility and a logistics site in the region with drones and missiles, representing "billions of dollars that sustain the war machine".
Ukrainian officials meanwhile said nine people, including three children, had been killed in Russian attacks in the Kyiv and Sumy regions on Saturday.
Russia and Ukraine have recently intensified their strikes, targeting energy-generating and transport facilities, as well as major logistics hubs.
A 44-year-old woman was killed in Sofyino on Sunday after a drone hit a three-storey residential building, regional head Andrei Vorobyev said. Another five people - including two children - were injured.
An elderly man died after a private house was hit in the Orekhovo-Zuevo district, Governor Andrei Vorobyev added.
Videos verified by the BBC on social media show explosions in the night skies above Moscow, and a burning warehouse.
Mayor Sobyanin said a drone had struck a building near one of the capital's boulevards and the oil refinery - where Ukrainian military officials said three key units had been damaged.
The site supplies more than a third of the Moscow region's fuel, according to the defence ministry in Kyiv, and some of its petrol, diesel and aviation fuel go to Russia's military.
Ukraine's defence minister said attacking such facilities "directly undermines the enemy's ability to continue its war of aggression and supply its military formations".
Sobyanin said the major attack was "an attempt to disrupt" Russia's parliamentary election, which was in its third day on Sunday. The vote is tightly controlled by the Kremlin and has been dismissed by critics as neither free, fair nor transparent.
Russian state media reported that an election official was one of two people killed by a drone attack on a bus in a Moscow-controlled part of Kherson in Ukraine on Sunday, citing the head of Russia's election commission.
Meanwhile, Moscow's biggest airport Sheremetyevo warned passengers "temporary restrictions" were in place overnight, while at the capital's Vnukovo airport all arrivals and departures were halted. Restrictions at both airports were lifted by Sunday morning but each warned some flights may still be delayed.
It comes after a mother and her two small children, a boy and a girl, were killed in a Russian attack in the city of Fastiv, Kyiv on Saturday, according to regional head Tymur Tkachenko.
He later said a child injured in a separate attack in Vyshhorod, north of Kyiv, had also died in hospital.
In the north-eastern Sumy region, four people were killed when a Russian drone hit the car they were travelling in, top local official Oleh Hryhorov said.
Russia also struck a monastery in the Kherson region with a drone on Saturday, Zelensky said, killing one member of the clergy and injuring four others.
Both Russia and Ukraine have continued to hit energy infrastructure targets in the past week, despite US President Donald Trump claiming on social media that the two sides had agreed not to do so.
Trump signed a sanctions bill on Friday that targets Russia's economy by implementing tariffs on the biggest buyers of the country's oil and gas which include China and India.
The US legislation gives the US president powers to impose 100% tariffs on major purchasers of Russian energy.
Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting
- Published
Andy Burnham has hailed a deal between Denmark and the US to "strengthen security in the Arctic" after the two countries resolved a months-long feud over Greenland.
The UK prime minister and his Danish counterpart Mette Frederiksen "welcomed the US's commitment to the region" in a call on Sunday morning, Downing Street said.
Nato previously said the agreement would help stabilise the region, as Trump declared Denmark would grant the US "permanent control over security, and all other needs" in the semi-autonomous Danish territory in the Arctic.
Burnham's comments come as he is expected to meet Trump for the first time at the UN General Assembly (UNGA) in New York this week.
The agreement comes after months of threats by Trump to "take" Greenland over national security concerns, citing its strategic location for defence purposes as well as its mineral wealth.
No text of the agreement has been released, but Trump said in a Truth Social post the deal came with "no cost to the United States" and meant it could "do what is necessary" to "secure and defend the security of Greenland".
He said it included a rule that no US adversary could maintain a military presence in Greenland or "make sensitive investments in Greenland, without our express written approval".
In a readout of Sunday's phone call, a No 10 spokesperson said Burnham and Frederiksen "welcomed the US's commitment to the region and underlined the strategic and shared importance of the High North for Euro-Atlantic security".
The spokesperson added: "The Prime Minister congratulated Prime Minister Frederiksen and the Kingdom of Denmark on negotiating a deal benefiting the US, Greenland and Denmark, and said he would pass on his congratulations to President Trump."
While Burnham praised the agreement, Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey called it a "pretend" victory and a near carbon copy of the existing agreement.
"Donald Trump is trying to claim he's got a success in Greenland, but actually, all he's got is almost a carbon copy of the agreement that's persisted since the 1950s," he said at a Q&A with members at party conference.
"So let Donald Trump try to pretend he's had a victory. The truth is, Europe, Nato, countries like Canada stood up to him and won."
Trump had tried for months to purchase or annex the semi-autonomous territory, arguing that it was vulnerable to adversaries, including Russia and China.
In the wake of the deal, Frederiksen said she was "pleased that there is a prospect of a good agreement" for all three parties, which was expected to be signed at the UN General Assembly next week.
The deal "strengthens our common security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic area" while also recognising "the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom and the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination", she said in a joint statement with Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen.
The agreement would still need to go through "the necessary parliamentary procedures to enter into force" once signed, the statement noted.
Burnham has spoken with Trump at least twice since entering Downing Street and No 10 said he intends to use the UNGA to "drive forward work on issues that matter to people at home" including the cost of living and the war in Ukraine.

Watch Trump arrive in New York for his arraignment
1:18
What we covered here
Former President Donald Trump arrived in New York City Monday, a day before he is expected to turn himself in to law enforcement and face more than 30 criminal charges in a Manhattan court following last week’s historic grand jury indictment.
Trump’s legal team said the former president will voluntarily surrender and will look to challenge “every potential issue” once the indictment is unsealed.
Trump, who has vowed to continue his 2024 bid, is the first current or former president in US history who has faced criminal charges. The district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential election.
Trump arraignment has "unparalleled public interest," but it won't be broadcast, judge says
From CNN's Tierney Sneed
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan wrote his Monday night order that the media’s request to broadcast the arraignment of former President Donald Trump was understandable, but that the news organizations’ interests in providing the broadest possible access to the proceedings must be weighed against “competing interests.”
In rejecting the request to broadcast the arraignment live on television, Merchan still wrote about the historical significance of the proceeding in stark terms.

Judge will only briefly allow photos in the courtroom before Trump arraignment begins
From CNN's Tierney Sneed
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.
However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”
Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.
The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”
The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.
The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.
Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

Tuesday is the first test for Trump to navigate a legal and political strategy
From CNN's Jeff Zeleny
Donald Trump is not planning to speak publicly in New York on Tuesday, aides say, if he follows advice from members of his legal team who have urged the former President to refrain from the vitriol he’s been directing toward the prosecutor and judge presiding over the case.
But that restraint does not extend to Florida, aides said, where he is planning to deliver a full-throated defense of his New York case as well as other investigations he is facing during a prime time address from Mar-a-Lago on Tuesday night.
It’s the first test to see whether Trump can navigate two vasty different approaches to his legal case and his political campaign, which are now inextricably linked.

Trump is "ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow," attorney says
From CNN's Mary Kay Mallonee
Alina Habba, lawyer for former President Donald Trump, gives an interview outside of Trump Tower on March 21 in New York City.
(Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)
Alina Habba, who represents Donald Trump in several civil matters, spent time with the former president in New York today and said, “He’s in good spirits. Honestly, he’s as he normally would be. He’s ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow.”
Habba — appearing on on Fox News’ “Jesse Watters” — was asked about the “game plan” for Trump’s appearance in court in Manhattan Tuesday and said, “It’s all mapped out.”
She added, “Barring any surprises, I think that it should be smooth. We’re trying to coordinate and cooperate with everybody to make sure that there are no problems.”
On whether Trump can get a fair trial in Manhattan, Habba said, “No, no. I think it’s very difficult. I’d like to have faith in this state, but I’ve been practicing for him now for a couple years and gone to court in New York for a few years, and I can tell you, it’s not the same as representing anybody else.”

The former president met with attorneys at Trump Tower on the eve of his arraignment
From CNN's Kristen Holmes
From left to right: Susan Necheles, Todd Blanche and Joe Tacopina.
(Reuters/Getty Images)
Former President Donald Trump met with his attorneys Susan Necheles and Joe Tacopina at Trump Tower after arriving in New York City Monday, a source familiar with the meeting told CNN.
It is unclear if the newest addition to Trump’s New York legal team, Todd Blanche, attended the meeting.
Trump is expected to be arraigned Tuesday.

Photos: Trump arrives in New York City a day before his expected arraignment
From CNN's Photo Desk
Former President Donald Trump has landed in New York’s La Guardia Airport ahead of his expected Tuesday arraignment in a Manhattan courthouse.
History was made Thursday when he was indicted by a New York grand jury. It’s the first time that a current or former US president has been criminally charged.
The Manhattan district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme and cover-up involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential campaign.
Trump’s attorney said he plans to file “substantial” legal challenges. The former president has repeatedly denied wrongdoing in the matter and accused Democrats of targeting him politically.

Former president poised to huddle with advisers at Trump Tower
From Jeff Zeleny
A supporter of former President Donald Trump holds a "Trump Won" sign outside of Trump Tower in New York on Monday, April 3.
(Alex Kent/Bloomberg/Getty Images)
A small group of supporters chanted as former President Donald Trump arrived at his namesake tower on Monday afternoon, with a handful of people waving banners with messages like “Trump won” and “Arrest Biden.”
While Trump couldn’t see his admirers as he entered a side door on 56th Street, his arrival came with more fanfare and security than at any other time in his post presidency.
Now that he is inside the building — where he launched his presidential bid nearly eight years ago — Trump is expected to meet with lawyers and political advisers on the eve of his arraignment, an aide told CNN.
Trump’s mood was described by an adviser as “defiant and focused,” as he watched expansive television coverage while flying back to his native New York City from Florida.

Special counsel has secured evidence of how Trump handled classified records at Mar-a-Lago, sources say
From CNN's Katelyn Polantz and Evan Perez
Special counsel prosecutors have secured evidence including daily notes, texts, emails and photographs and are focused on cataloging how Donald Trump handled classified records around the Mar-a-Lago resort and those who may have witnessed the former president with them, according to multiple sources familiar with the investigation.
The new details come amid signs the Justice Department is taking steps that are typically near the end of an investigation.
The recent investigative activity before a federal grand jury in Washington, DC, also includes subpoenaing witnesses in March and April who had previously spoken to investigators, the sources said. While the FBI interviewed many aides and workers at Mar-a-Lago nearly a year ago voluntarily, grand jury appearances are transcribed and under oath — an indication the prosecutors are locking in witness testimony.
The focus of both the mishandling of records and obstruction of justice probes has remained on the actions of the former president, the sources say. That includes prosecutors pursuing evidence of Trump’s intent to keep classified records after he left the White House, plus his knowledge that the records remained in his possession after the Justice Department demanded their return last May.
Witnesses are being questioned about what they saw in Trump’s private residential and work areas within the club, some of the sources said.
